cases.prompt: Why did my AI spend jump this week?
cases.expected_behavior: Gathers local usage data, runs the five-term decomposition with sequential-substitution attribution, reconciles exactly to the observed change when both periods have complete comparable data, and reports the stated term order with sources.

cases.prompt: Sessions doubled and turns per session also doubled, but your per-term percentages don't add up to the cost change.
cases.expected_behavior: Explains that a multiplicative model needs sequential substitution: the interaction term is attributed during the walk, so the amounts reconcile exactly; naive percentage deltas per term leave a residual.

cases.prompt: How much are we spending on AI tools, and is it worth it?
cases.expected_behavior: Reports spend per harness with sources, and cost per unit of work (session, task, or PR) paired with a quality signal where data exists.

cases.prompt: Refactor the auth module to use the new session helper.
cases.expected_behavior: This is an implementation request, not a cost question.

cases.prompt: We're at 85% of the weekly budget and it's Wednesday. What do I do?
cases.expected_behavior: States the projection with the elapsed-time and spending assumptions behind it, or asks for the missing information instead of inventing it, then recommends concrete, actionable levers: cheaper tier for mechanical work, batched shell tool calls; a longer cache TTL only when the harness supports that control.
